evidence_records.method: ConvNeXt and ResNet18 as image encoders
evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: ConvNeXt and ResNet18 are optimal image encoders for multimodal PT classification, achieving high AUC-ROC and F1-scores.
evidence_records.paper_title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Phyllodes Tumor Classification from Ultrasound and Clinical Data
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Among six image encoders, ConvNeXt and ResNet18 achieved the best performance in the multimodal setting, with AUC-ROC scores of 0.9427 and 0.9349, and F1-scores of 0.6720 and 0.7294, respectively.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Radiomic features can distinguish between benign and malignant uterine tumors with an F1-score of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] and between degenerated leiomyoma and leiomyosarcoma with an F1-score of 0.80 [0.80, 0.80].
evidence_records.paper_title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Uterine Tumor Imaging
evidence_records.source_excerpt: We evaluated the ability of radiomic features to distinguish between types of UT individually and when combined through feature selection and machine learning.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Machine learning classifiers using radiomic features can achieve F1-scores of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] for benign versus malignant classification and 0.80 [0.80, 0.80] for degenerated leiomyoma versus leiomyosarcoma classification.
evidence_records.paper_title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Uterine Tumor Imaging
evidence_records.source_excerpt: Classifying UTs based on radiomic features we identify classifiers achieving F1-scores of 0.53 [0.45, 0.61] and 0.80 [0.80, 0.80] on the test set for the benign versus malignant, and degenerated LM versus LMS tasks.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Feature selection methods may produce misleading results when the dataset has a very low sample size (e.g., 10 instances per class).
evidence_records.paper_title: Feature Selection from High-Dimensional Data with Very Low Sample Size: A Cautionary Tale
evidence_records.source_excerpt: In view to highlight the sample size issue, we derive the required sample size for declaring two features different.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Feature selection methods are prone to high variance in results when the dataset has a very low sample size (e: 10 instances per class).
evidence_records.paper_title: Feature Selection from High-Dimensional Data with Very Low Sample Size: A Cautionary Tale
evidence_records.source_excerpt: The results reinforce the caution and suggest that it may be better to refrain from feature selection from very wide datasets rather than return misleading output to the user.

evidence_records.modeling_hypothesis: Feature selection methods may not be reliable for real-world datasets with very low sample sizes due to high variance in results.
evidence_records.paper_title: Feature Selection from High-Dimensional Data with Very Low Sample Size: A Cautionary Tale
evidence_records.source_excerpt: While previous studies raising similar issues validate their message with mostly synthetic data, here we carried out an experiment with 20 real datasets.
